subject.title: fix: stop doctor misreporting trusted-proxy gateways as unauthenticated

question: Should Doctor classify a non-loopback Gateway as authenticated only after the proposed runtime-aligned trusted-proxy, origin, and startup-auth checks succeed, with exec SecretRefs still requiring explicit `--allow-exec`?
rationale: This changes the operator-facing security diagnosis and governs when Doctor is permitted to invoke configured secret providers; tests and recordings support mechanics but cannot substitute for the repository owner’s intended security posture.

options.title: Approve the bounded diagnostic model
options.body: Keep the runtime-aligned readiness path, require a refreshed current-head proof, and merge only after the rebase confirms the final security behavior.

options.title: Keep the current unauthenticated critical
options.body: Reject the warning downgrade and retain the existing conservative Doctor classification for every exposed trusted-proxy configuration.

recommendation.title: Approve the bounded diagnostic model
recommendation.body: Keep the runtime-aligned readiness path, require a refreshed current-head proof, and merge only after the rebase confirms the final security behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: A current-main Gateway/auth owner needs to be identified from local repository history before the security-boundary decision is routed.
